assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with cardiovascular and renal benefit now shown in large outcome trials. The concept is clear, the chain from peptide biology to drug is well documented, and the impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, mechanism of action) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) are the most defensible three. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is also plausible and the credit is crowded, so a three-person cap forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Mature: approved drugs since 2005, with decades of independent confirmation and outcome data. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit split between basic discoverers, peptide chemists and industrial drug developers is contested; Mojsov's priority is debated.
Long-term safety and the mechanism of central appetite effects are still being studied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed at tumour antigens opened a new therapeutic modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and myeloma. The idea is original, clinically decisive and has spawned a field.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation) and June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) are central; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR trials. Eshhar and others are not on the supplied credit list, which leaves attribution incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 with multi-year follow-up showing cures in a subset. Timing is good, though the solid-tumour problem and toxicity remain.
uncertainties: Foundational contributions by people outside the supplied credit list.
Durability and long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, are still maturing.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity, and it has become a standard tool across the field and has also reached early clinical use in vision restoration. Originality and breadth of impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Boyden and Deisseroth established its use in neurons, with Miesenboeck an earlier conceptual precursor. Six credited names force a choice. A three-person configuration of two discoverers and one neuronal implementer is defensible but excludes several with strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than 15 years of broad independent use and validation. Clinical translation is only beginning.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal implementation is disputed.
Tool-type discovery may be judged against disease-relevant discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one, and established a clear, generalisable principle for splice-modulating therapeutics in neurological disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2 exon 7 inclusion) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a coherent pair. Adrian Krainer and Bennett's collaborators in the Ionis effort are not individually separable from the supplied names; Hua, Singh and Biogen colleagues are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with long-term follow-up in infants and children. Timing is reasonable and the finding is robust.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as recognising splicing biology or ASO chemistry.
Contributions of other co-inventors not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting CML from a fatal into a chronically managed disease. Impact and clarity are exemplary.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical proof and development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are a natural three. The earlier work on the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Groffen, Heisterkamp, Witte) is outside this credit set and raises the question of whether the discovery has been partly recognised.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with 20+ years of survival data, though the prize may feel late relative to the earliest events.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier-recognised cancer genetics could lower the novelty of the claim.
Previously recognised via Lasker; novelty relative to earlier prizes is a consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data now show large reductions in cervical cancer incidence. This is a major preventive-medicine achievement building on the HPV-cancer link already recognised.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP assembly and immunogenicity), and Frazer (parallel VLP work and vaccine development) are the standard trio; Jian Zhou (Frazer's collaborator) is not credited here and priority between the groups has been discussed.
assessment.maturity: Vaccines licensed in 2006 with real-world effectiveness now demonstrated; the cancer-incidence evidence is increasingly strong, supporting timing.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among VLP developers and the omission of Jian Zhou.
Industrial development by Merck and GSK also contributed to the translation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus is an effective therapy for motor complications in Parkinson's disease and has been extended to tremor and dystonia. It is a clinically decisive neurological intervention, assessed here as a practising neurologist but not as a preference for the field.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the credited name; his contribution of high-frequency thalamic and subthalamic stimulation is clear. Other contributors, including those who established the basal ganglia model and the subthalamic target, are not in the credit set, so a one-person configuration may under-represent the field.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of use and randomised trials. Symptomatic rather than disease-modifying.
uncertainties: Credit set is a single name and does not cover related basal ganglia circuit work.
Symptomatic benefit only; mechanism of action is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as the molecular constituents of neurofibrillary tangles, Lewy bodies and related filaments reframed neurodegeneration around protein assembly, and underlies cryo-EM structural classification and seed-amplification diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini form a coherent pair, with the alpha-synuclein finding in Lewy bodies and the tau work in paired helical filaments. Contributions by Wischik and by Lee and Trojanowski on related tau and synuclein pathology are not in the credit set, and the overlap needs scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and now enabling diagnostics and structural classification. Therapeutic validation is still limited, so recognition may be somewhat early on clinical impact.
uncertainties: Priority relative to other groups working on tau and synuclein pathology.
